batch_strategy: matched strength and loading contrasts with structural controls

choices.reason: A high-strength m72 DCM probe samples a broad predicted V1/V2 regime and extends the scaffold response into a condition region where nonlinear onset and finish behavior may emerge.
This m3 5/1 DCM row supplies a chemically distinct high-width V2 calibration point and tests whether a compact donor-free aromatic scaffold follows the ordinary regime.
A compact m55 ester-like control at high strength anchors ordinary central-distribution behavior against the difficult late-retention probes.
The low-strength m54 control has a narrow predicted regime and low feature-space distance, providing a useful ordinary anchor for both endpoints.
This m29 high-strength carbonyl-containing row has a comparatively broad predicted interval and tests local strength response in a simple aromatic ketone environment.
A high-strength donor-free m9 condition provides a compact structural control for separating genuine late tails from broad model extrapolation.
This molecule-novel m169 condition probes a chlorinated carbonyl scaffold at weak strength, adding structural coverage near the compact regime.
The m182 weak-strength condition tests a fused carbonyl-containing scaffold with a broad predicted V2 range, helping calibrate transfer outside the most sampled families.
A low-strength m125 anchor is useful for separating a scaffold-wide late-retention tendency from a strength-triggered transition and for calibrating onset versus finish.
This m43 high-strength halogenated ketone condition samples a moderately broad predicted regime and provides a donor-free carbonyl control.
The m50 50/1 PE row is predicted to remain compact despite extreme solvent strength, making it a useful test of ordinary halogenated behavior and global strength corrections.
This weak-strength m184 aldehyde-like condition is a compact control that helps identify whether broad predictions in related halogenated rows correspond to actual finish tails.
A narrow m109 1/1 condition provides an ordinary aromatic ether control at intermediate loading and prevents tail corrections from spreading across all heteroatom-containing rows.
The m84 condition has a broad predicted V2 interval and tests finish-tail calibration in an ester-like halogenated scaffold at high strength.
This m79 high-strength DCM row probes a predicted onset shift in a compact ester-like molecule and helps locate a possible strength transition.
This m72 2/1 point forms a local lower-strength contrast with the selected m72 5/1 row, allowing onset and finish slopes to be learned from the same scaffold.
The m89 2/1 PE condition samples a moderate predicted regime for a donor-containing aromatic ester and helps connect compact and late-response families.
A high-strength m34 PE row with broad endpoint widths tests whether a simple halogenated ketone develops a local tail under stronger elution conditions.
This weak-strength m69 ketone condition is a compact ordinary control that anchors the lower side of carbonyl-rich behavior.
The m167 high-strength diketone-like scaffold has a broad predicted V2 regime and directly adds finish-tail calibration for a multifunctional carbonyl environment.
A high-strength m2 halogenated hydrocarbon condition provides a relatively compact donor-free control against broad predictions in polar and multifunctional rows.
This m81 high-strength ester-like condition has a broad predicted interval and probes whether the model transfers the late-tail response to a less polar carbonyl scaffold.
The m142 5/1 aldehyde condition samples a broad intermediate-strength regime and helps calibrate carbonyl onset and finish without relying only on extreme rows.
A second m184 strength condition creates a local contrast with the weak-strength m184 control, testing whether its predicted interval expands with solvent strength.
This m213 high-strength ether-rich condition adds structural exploration in a moderate predicted regime and tests transfer beyond the measured late carbonyl families.
The m7 50/1 DCM condition is a high-strength donor-free control for testing whether extreme mobile-phase composition alone produces a late tail.
A weak-strength m143 aldehyde-like row provides a compact halogenated carbonyl anchor and protects central-distribution accuracy.
This m92 EA condition probes cross-solvent-system transfer in a high-strength regime, where both onset and finish corrections may differ from DCM and PE.
The m38 2/1 DCM row supplies a compact intermediate-strength anchor for a fused carbonyl scaffold with potentially condition-sensitive tails.
This m197 2/1 PE aldehyde condition samples a broad predicted V2 regime and adds direct finish calibration in a donor-containing aromatic family.
A weak-strength hydrocarbon control with a narrow predicted interval helps constrain ordinary nonpolar behavior and prevents indiscriminate late-retention correction.
The m192 2/1 halogenated aldehyde condition provides another intermediate-strength V2 calibration point with a distinct loading and structural environment.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-strength response and onset/finish coupling remain scaffold-specific, with nonlinear transition locations and slopes that cannot be represented reliably by one global PE/EA trend.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched local strength probes can teach transition positions and slopes that generalize across related structures without imposing a global solvent correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do nearby functional-group families share transition locations after loading is controlled, or are the transitions still scaffold-specific?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading-solvent conditions alter V1 and V2 differently across scaffolds, so mass alone is insufficient as a universal loading correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts can separate onset displacement from finish-tail expansion and improve interaction terms involving loading and solvent strength.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed molecule and PE/EA ratio, does loading mainly shift V1, expand V2, or do both effects vary by scaffold?

hypotheses.content: V2 and interval width require direct local calibration; predicted quantile width is useful for finding probes but is not generally calibrated for finish-tail behavior.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Direct V2 labels across compact, intermediate, and broad predicted regimes can teach when interval width reflects a true tail rather than model extrapolation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can structural descriptors identify finish width across families, or are local scaffold-condition anchors still required?

hypotheses.content: Late-retention failures cluster across heteroatom-rich, carbonyl-rich, heteroaromatic, and multifunctional scaffolds, but their transition locations remain local.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Family-diverse difficult rows can expose transferable structural signals while preserving local transition boundaries and reducing systematic underprediction of late V2.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which local structural environments best identify entry into late V2 behavior?

hypotheses.content: Donor-free, halogenated, and compact acceptor-only rows are not one uniform behavior class; ordinary controls are needed alongside difficult rows to prevent indiscriminate tail correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controls distinguish genuine late-retention chemistry from compact exceptions, protecting accuracy across the central Row-distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which donor-free and acceptor-only environments remain compact across strength and loading, and which produce delayed onset or long tails?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback strengthens the local-response interpretation while weakening reliance on predicted width alone. The m107 sequence showed monotone onset growth with strongly nonlinear V2 expansion. The m177 outcomes contrasted compact and broad-tail conditions, supporting separate onset and finish calibration. Several broad predictions were nevertheless compact or shifted in onset, while donor-free and halogenated controls continued to show heterogeneous behavior. The next batch therefore emphasizes matched strength contrasts, direct V2 calibration, and ordinary controls alongside structurally diverse probes.
batch_rationale: The batch combines paired m72 conditions with broad and compact structural controls, intermediate and high-strength carbonyl probes, cross-solvent-system measurements, and several ordinary donor-free or halogenated anchors. The direct V2 probes target finish-tail behavior across ester, aldehyde, diketone, and heteroatom-rich environments. The compact controls protect the central Row-distribution while the broader and structurally distinct rows test transfer into failure regions. Together these labels should improve local condition-response representation, loading and strength interactions, and structural generalization for both V1 and V2.
